title: Bounded-below derived smooth base change
statement:
In the square of
[sbc-thm-smooth-base-change] with $f$ smooth, $g$ quasi-compact
and quasi-separated, and $\mathcal P$ the set of primes invertible on
$S$: for $K\in D^+_{\mathcal P\text{-tor}}(T_{\Et})$,

$$
{\operatorname{BC}}_{f,g}(K):Lf^*Rg_*K\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Rh_*Le^*K
$$

in $D^+_{\mathcal P\text{-tor}}(X_{\Et})$.

proof.text: Choose a lower bound a for K. For each n, Kn = tau_le_n K has the same Hq as K for q <= n and zero above n, by the standard truncation triangle. It is bounded between a and n, including the case n < a, and its cohomology remains allowable torsion.

proof.text: Apply bounded allowable-torsion smooth base change to Kn. For any triangulated functor F preserving lower bounds, apply F to the standard triangle tau_le_n K -> K -> tau_gt_n K. The last term remains >= n+1, so its H^(n-1) and H^n vanish, and the long exact sequence makes H^n(F(tau_le_n K)) -> H^n(F(K)) invertible. Both Rg followed by exact inverse image and exact inverse image followed by Rh preserve lower bounds, by rightDerivedFunctorPlusCompatibility and exact-functor compatibility. Apply this elementary truncation-triangle argument to both sides of the exchange. Naturality of abelianDerivedBaseChangeTransformation gives a commutative square on H^n. Its two vertical maps and its bounded exchange are invertible, so the remaining exchange is invertible. DerivedCategory.isIso_iff detects the resulting ambient isomorphism. This does not use the spectral-sequence support clause of sbc-lem-bounded-below-truncation-criterion.

proof.text: To apply qcqs_higherDirectImages_prime_torsion at a separably closed geometric point s, extend its field to its algebraic closure. The already-proved Scheme.isIso_pointSmallEtalePrecomp_sheafFiber gives an additive stalk isomorphism for this field extension. Transport annihilators across this isomorphism. This uses the existing algebraically closed formulation without changing that statement.

proof.text: For a sheaf F placed in degree zero, qcqs higher direct images preserve allowable torsion by the preceding step. The proved rightDerivedFunctorPlusCompatibility identifies plus and unbounded right derived functors. Negative cohomology vanishes by left exactness. More generally, if K is bounded below at a, repackage it as a plus object and use the same compatibility to show Rg(K) is bounded below at a.

proof.text: The allowable-torsion plus class is triangulated and closed under isomorphisms. Its inverse image under the triangulated functor Rg is therefore such a class. Apply the already-proved DerivedCategory.prop_of_bounded (WeilConjectures/Mathlib/Algebra/Homology/DerivedCategory/TStructure.lean) to Kn: single sheaves satisfy this class by step 4, and Hq(Kn) is allowable by the truncation API. Hence all Hq(Rg(Kn)) have allowable torsion. After applying Rg to the standard triangle Kn -> K -> tau_gt_n K, its third term is >= n+1 by step 4. The long exact sequence shows Hn(Rg(Kn)) -> Hn(Rg(K)) is an isomorphism. Transport the allowable property. This is bounded devissage plus truncation in place of the optional hypercohomology filtration.

proof.text: Exact inverse image commutes with cohomology and preserves lower bounds. The shared lemma [lem-sbc-allowable-torsion-upper-star], formerly private to this module, identifies its geometric stalk with the original stalk at the composite geometric point and transports allowable annihilators across this additive isomorphism. Thus Lf*Rg*K is bounded below with allowable-torsion cohomology. The ambient isomorphism of step 2 transports this property to Rh*Le*K, completing all three conjuncts.
